You are given an array $$T$$ of size $$n$$. Count the number of arrays $$S$$ such that Simons can transform $$S$$ to $$T$$, modulo $$998\,244\,353$$.

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 8000$$$). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line contains an integer $$n$$ ($$1$\leq n\leq 8000$$$) — the length of $$T$$.

The second line contains $$n$$ integers $$T_1,T_2,\ldots,T_n$$ ($$1$\leq T_i\leq 8000$$$) — the elements of $$T$$.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $$n$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$8000$$.

For each test case, output a single integer — the number of arrays $$S$$, modulo $$998\,244\,353$$.
